claims.claim: Three invocation paths: (A) automatic description-match, (B) manual /slash command, (C) Skill tool programmatic. Each path has distinct permission controls.
claims.evidence: Official docs three invocation paths section.

claims.claim: Path A (automatic) selection mechanism is pure LLM forward pass against skill descriptions; there is no regex, no keyword matching, no scoring algorithm exposed to users.
claims.evidence: Absence of documented selection heuristic; community reverse-engineering consensus.

claims.claim: Path A effectiveness depends on description trigger richness: generic descriptions (helps with X) rarely fire; specific with keywords (programmatic video generation, animation timing) fire reliably.
claims.evidence: R7 premium skills pattern (Remotion example) + community troubleshooting reports.

claims.claim: Path B (manual) activated via /skill-name in Claude Code CLI; supports argument passing via $ARGUMENTS substitution.
claims.evidence: Docs slash command syntax + string substitutions.

claims.claim: In Claude Code 2.1+, custom commands and skills are merged: both .claude/commands/name.md and .claude/skills/name/SKILL.md create /name command; skill wins on conflict.
Path C (Skill tool) allows agents/skills to invoke other skills programmatically; invocation is recorded as Skill tool call in conversation, not as user slash command.
claims.evidence: Official Skill tool docs + conversation trace analysis.

claims.claim: Permission rules syntax for Skill tool: Skill (deny-all), Skill(exact-name), Skill(name-prefix *), supported in both allow and deny rule sets in settings.
claims.evidence: Restrict Claude skill access section docs.

claims.claim: Priority matrix: disable-model-invocation:true blocks path A and C (auto + Skill tool); user-invocable:false blocks only path B visibility (auto and Skill tool unaffected).
Argument passing: Path B supports positional args ($0, $1) and full string ($ARGUMENTS); Path A cannot pass args (Claude generates call); Path C passes args via Skill tool input schema.
claims.evidence: String substitutions docs + Skill tool schema.

claims.claim: Bug #17283: when skill with context:fork + agent fields is invoked via Skill tool, fork isolation does not occur; skill runs in caller's context silently.
Live change detection applies to all three invocation paths; modifying skill during active session is reflected immediately in next invocation.
SDK invocation differences: Claude Agent SDK supports paths A and C but not B (slash commands are Claude Code UI feature); allowed-tools field is also Claude Code-specific.
claims.evidence: SDK docs comparison with Claude Code.

claims.claim: Built-in commands accessible via Skill tool: /init, /review, /security-review. Other built-ins (e.g., /compact) are NOT invokable programmatically.
Plugin skills use namespace in all three paths: /plugin-name:skill-name (B), description with namespace in listing (A), Skill(plugin-name:skill-name) (C).
Skill invocation is recorded as single message in conversation trace; after invocation, content persists for remainder of session (not re-read on subsequent turns).
Auto-invocation (path A) is gated by skill description appearing in system prompt; disable-model-invocation removes description, eliminating path A eligibility.

Manual invocation via /name works even when description is removed from context (disable-model-invocation:true); Claude Code scans skill directory for slash command availability independently of description injection.
claims.evidence: Official behavior table row 2 (disable-model-invocation:true / You invoke: Yes).

claims.claim: Invocation cost breakdown: path A pays pre-invocation reasoning + skill body tokens; path B pays slash resolution + skill body; path C pays Skill tool schema + skill body. Body tokens identical across paths.

conflicts_flagged.description: Auto vs manual reliability trade-off: automatic invocation saves user effort but has non-deterministic trigger; manual is 100% deterministic but requires memorization of skill names.
Skill tool built-in coverage gap: /compact accessible to user but not to agents, preventing programmatic context management in long-running chains.

gaps_flagged.description: No latency benchmark published for path A (description match reasoning) vs path B (direct resolution); community assumes path A adds 1-3s overhead.
Interaction between paths field (glob filter) and path A: does a skill with paths: ['src/**/*.ts'] get included in description listing globally or only when editing matching files? Unclear.

summary: R3 systematizes 3 invocation paths with permission/argument/SDK differences, documents merged commands+skills semantics (2.1+), and flags Bug #17283 affecting Skill tool fork behavior. Auto-invocation is pure LLM decision (no regex), depends on description quality.
